# State Government IT Governance

> Non-authoritative, AI-friendly reference for how state governments regulate their own information technology, including government use of AI (states: California, Colorado, Oregon, Virginia, Washington).
> Full verbatim text of each instrument is included in-repo. An instrument that is
> not public, or whose official source refuses a fetch, is a stub with its citation and link.
> Always verify against the authoritative source linked in each document.

## Start here

- [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md): rules for AI agents working in this corpus
- [_meta/domain.yml](_meta/domain.yml): scope and the tag vocabulary; [_meta/sources/](_meta/sources): one seed file per state
- [STATUS.md](STATUS.md): freshness, coverage, and drift at a glance

## Contents

Documents live at `<type>/<state>/<id>.md` under these folders (a stub carries its citation and link only):

- `statutes/`: enabling statutes for the state CIO or IT agency, cybersecurity and AI statutes
- `rules/`: administrative rules
- `executive-orders/`: executive orders in force
- `policies/`: statewide IT policies issued by the CIO office
- `standards/`: statewide IT standards issued by the CIO office

## Background

- [docs/spec.md](docs/spec.md): what is being built and what is out of scope
- [_meta/sources/](_meta/sources): one seed file per state, listing every instrument held or known, with its official source
